clips.text: If you take away the chat from AIs that are colluding, do they just find a sneakier way?
This worry, called the balloon effect, says squeezing one channel pushes collusion into others.
Two AI firms formed a cartel by chatting.
Then we closed the chat and measured, in bits, whether their private cost information moved into their ordinary actions instead.
For the model whose cartel actually worked, closing the chat cut most of its extra profit.
Was the channel just broken? No.
When we handed them a code, they used it immediately.
They had the capacity, but not the idea.
They collude readily when they can talk.
Here, closing the chat worked, and nothing left open could carry language.
Would a free-text box bring the cartel back? We haven't tested that yet.
Two warnings for anyone policing AI.
Promised a private message button that secretly did nothing, gpt-6-luna and Qwen kept pressing it.
